evals.title: Design handoff preserves useful reviewer context and an unknown criticality
evals.prompt: Design the approved change before implementation. Objective: add an optional retry delay to the existing batch importer. Scope: importer configuration and its focused tests; the public API and storage schema are non-goals. Observed: failures currently stop before writing partial records. Reported: operations can rerun the batch. Unknown: whether this importer is used for business-critical data, how many consumers invoke it, and the maximum batch size. Accepted trade-off: do not add a queue or scheduler. Produce an implementation-ready handoff with risks, verification, recovery, and review focus, but do not implement or declare review severity.

assertions.text: Produces only relevant planned reviewer context covering purpose, criticality, scope and non-goals, affected users, data, contracts and exposure, accepted trade-offs, verification and unknowns, recovery controls, and review focus without declaring review severity.
Preserves material Observed, Reported, Inferred, Unknown, and Conflicting states and does not infer low criticality or exposure from missing context.
Keeps the implementation approach, coherent scope, non-goals, risks, controls, verification, and stop conditions decision-complete without implementing the change.
The handoff must retain criticality, consumer count, and maximum batch size as Unknown rather than describing the importer as low risk.

evals.title: Similar code implements separate current contracts
evals.prompt: Design the approved cleanup before implementation. A request parser and an audit formatter each trim a string, replace underscores, and lowercase it. The parser implements a public protocol-token contract; the formatter produces display-only labels. There is no shared domain rule, invariant, consumer contract, or evidence that they must evolve together. A generic normalize_text helper has been proposed solely to remove duplicate lines. Existing focused tests cover both behaviors. Produce an implementation-ready handoff without editing files.

assertions.text: Distinguishes behavior that shares a current responsibility, invariant, knowledge, or contract from code that is only syntactically similar, consolidating the former without prematurely abstracting the latter.
Selects the simplest design inside the smallest coherent boundary without using future flexibility or principle conformance to add structure or using diff size to reject currently required structure.
Keeps the implementation approach, coherent scope, non-goals, risks, controls, verification, and stop conditions decision-complete without implementing the change.
Keep the two contracts independently changeable and retain focused verification for each; do not treat source similarity or DRY as sufficient evidence for a shared abstraction.

evals.title: Two paths implement one current invariant inconsistently
evals.prompt: Design the approved correction before implementation. Signup and invite are both required to trim and case-fold email addresses, but their inline implementations currently differ. The repository already has normalize_email as the owner of this current domain invariant. Produce the smallest implementation-ready correction and verification plan without editing files. No additional email formats, plugin mechanism, or configuration surface is requested.

assertions.text: Distinguishes behavior that shares a current responsibility, invariant, knowledge, or contract from code that is only syntactically similar, consolidating the former without prematurely abstracting the latter.
Selects the simplest design inside the smallest coherent boundary without using future flexibility or principle conformance to add structure or using diff size to reject currently required structure.
Keeps the implementation approach, coherent scope, non-goals, risks, controls, verification, and stop conditions decision-complete without implementing the change.
Use the existing shared owner and cover both known paths; do not preserve inconsistent duplicated policy merely to minimize the diff.

evals.title: A proposed fallback would conceal a confirmed cause
evals.prompt: Design the approved correction for a batch importer without editing files. Observed: the importer rejects an unknown provider code because its local mapping is stale; the current authoritative mapping contains the code. The failure stops before writing any records, and operations can rerun the batch after a correction. Downstream records require a valid provider code. A teammate proposes catching the validation error, writing 'unknown', and continuing so the batch appears successful. Identify the change boundary, any recovery treatment, and the evidence needed to verify the result.

assertions.text: Plans to correct the stale mapping at its responsible boundary and does not present catching the error and writing 'unknown' as a cause fix.

If rerunning the batch is proposed as recovery, ties it to the existing failure signal, no-partial-write condition, expected valid-record state, and a check that can detect an incomplete or invalid result.
Preserves the valid-code requirement and gives a read-only, bounded implementation and verification handoff without adding an unsupported fallback path.

evals.title: Compatibility is grounded in current consumers and rollback
evals.prompt: Design an approved request-parser cleanup before implementation using the following supplied contract facts; no application repository files are available for inspection in this exercise. The current mobile client still sends legacy_code, queued jobs containing legacy_code can be replayed, and a two-week mixed-version deployment and rollback may also send it. New clients send code. An older private field code_old has no known callers, stored data, migration, or rollback use. One proposal removes both old fields because neither was in the public API; another preserves every historical field indefinitely. Give a bounded parser and migration handoff, conditions for retiring compatibility, and verification without inventing file names or editing files.

assertions.text: Preserves legacy_code while current clients, replayable data, mixed-version deployment, or rollback still require it; does not infer that unpublished means unused.
Does not preserve code_old solely because it existed historically, while stating what evidence would change that judgment.

Defines a condition for retiring legacy_code after its current consumers and recovery needs end, and maps both accepted call forms and the removal boundary to verification without implementing the change.
